questions.stem: Why does a language model need tools when building a software solution?

options.A: To retrain itself overnight on every private company document set
options.B: To reach live data, exact maths, or outside actions
options.C: To replace all application code with free-form generated text only
options.D: To store permanent memories of every previous user conversation

questions.rationale: Models generate language from context. Tools give the surrounding application controlled ways to fetch data, compute values, or change external systems.

questions.stem: Does the language model itself execute an approved tool call against an external system?
questions.rationale: The model proposes a structured tool call. Application code validates, authorizes, executes, and returns the result.

questions.stem: What is function calling, also called tool calling, in a generative AI system?

options.A: A direct network call the model opens to any public website address
options.B: A silent rewrite of the model weights during a live user session
options.C: A database trigger that scores every generated sentence in storage
options.D: A structured request for a named capability the code may run

questions.rationale: Function calling is a structured proposal from the model. The application decides whether and how to run the named capability.

questions.stem: Is a model-generated tool call by itself enough evidence that the external action succeeded?
questions.rationale: Only a verified tool result from the application supports a success claim. A proposed call is not proof of execution.

questions.stem: What should a reliable tool contract include for the model and the surrounding code?

options.A: An open prompt that lets the model invent any argument shape it likes
options.B: A shared password that students embed inside generated answer text
options.C: A clear name, description, input schema, and output shape
options.D: A promise that every call will succeed without any validation step

questions.rationale: Clear names, decision-boundary descriptions, narrow schemas, and predictable outputs reduce ambiguous or unsafe calls.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly describes the five-stage tool-calling lifecycle?

options.A: Offer tools, get a call, run it in code, return data, finish or loop
options.B: Train the model, publish weights, skip checks, then trust every claim
options.C: Store prompts, delete logs, disable timeouts, and allow every tool
options.D: Rank the slides, shuffle days, unlock grades, and hide the rationale

questions.rationale: The cycle is: send the request with tools, receive a tool call, execute in the application, return the result, then get a final answer or another call.

questions.stem: Does JSON Schema validation alone replace authorization and human approval for consequential actions?
questions.rationale: Schema checks argument shape. Semantic validation, permissions, and approval gates are still required for risky actions.

questions.stem: Which tool type usually needs the strongest controls before it runs?

options.A: A read tool that fetches a published policy paragraph from storage
options.B: A compute tool that totals a prepared list of invoice line amounts
options.C: A write tool that submits a payment or updates a record
options.D: A retrieval tool that searches an approved knowledge index set

questions.rationale: Write tools change external state. They need stricter authorization, previews, and often human approval.

questions.stem: When is it safest to run several tool operations at the same time?

options.A: When one operation must consume the output of another first
options.B: When two write tools target the same account balance row
options.C: When approval is still pending for a high-risk write action
options.D: When the operations are independent and do not conflict

questions.rationale: Independent reads or computations can run together. Dependent or conflicting actions should stay sequential.

questions.stem: Should a fully known, fixed business process start as a deterministic workflow rather than an open agent loop?
questions.rationale: Known sequences belong in application-controlled workflows. Agents help when intermediate evidence changes the next step.

questions.stem: What does the ReAct pattern combine inside a controlled agent loop?

options.A: Offline chunking paired with permanent model fine-tuning jobs
options.B: Reasoning steps with tool actions and later observations
options.C: Random tool choice with unrestricted outbound network access
options.D: Slide narration paired with automatic grade submission hooks

questions.rationale: ReAct interleaves reasoning, tool actions, and observations so the agent can update its next step from evidence.

questions.stem: When is Plan-and-Execute often a better fit than a short ReAct loop?

options.A: When work needs an ordered multi-step plan first
options.B: When a single lookup answers the user with one tool call alone
options.C: When no tool is allowed and only free text may be returned
options.D: When the system must avoid logging any intermediate run state

questions.rationale: Plan-and-Execute first builds a plan, then carries out steps. It fits longer tasks that need structured sequencing.

questions.stem: Which control most directly stops an agent from looping without bound?

options.A: A larger context window paired with no timeout settings at all
options.B: A warmer sampling temperature used only for creative wording
options.C: A longer system prompt that still omits allowed-tool lists
options.D: A maximum-step limit with clear stopping rules

questions.rationale: Maximum steps, budgets, timeouts, and stopping conditions keep the loop predictable and finite.

questions.stem: Should consequential write actions use preview and meaningful human confirmation before execution?
questions.rationale: Human-in-the-loop gates protect high-impact actions. Preview and confirmation reduce irreversible mistakes.

questions.stem: What is the main job of a routing pattern in a multi-skill assistant?

options.A: Direct each request to the fitting specialist path
options.B: Merge every tool into one unrestricted mega-function entry
options.C: Disable tracing so later inspection of routes is impossible
options.D: Force every request through the same write tool first

questions.rationale: Routing classifies the request and directs it to the right specialist workflow or tool set.

questions.stem: Which design best matches a reliable controlled agent for a course assistant?

options.A: Open tools, no step limit, and silent writes into student records
options.B: Narrow tools, clear state, budgets, traces, and stop rules
options.C: Hidden prompts, skipped checks, and unverified success claims
options.D: One giant tool that can email, pay, and delete without review

questions.rationale: Reliable agents combine flexible decisions with narrow tools, visible state, budgets, guardrails, tracing, and clear stopping rules.

questions.stem: What should evaluation measure beyond whether the final answer sounds fluent?

options.A: Only the character count of the generated rationale paragraph
options.B: Only how often the model avoids calling any available tool
options.C: Tool choice, arguments, recovery, safety, cost, and claims
options.D: Only whether the student interface used a dark colour theme

questions.rationale: Agent evaluation must check tool selection, argument quality, execution, recovery, task success, safety, latency, cost, and false claims of success.
